note:
Fourteen measured regions over ten of nineteen pages, all accounted for: thirteen rows - six figures and seven tables - plus one excluded region, no refusals and no unmeasured exhibit. The paper numbers six figures and seven tables and all thirteen own a region, so this is the first paper in the lane with no ghost grid. Every table is a closed box: full-height vertical rules at every column boundary plus a horizontal rule on every row, 4 to 7 rules across and 5 to 17 down, so the whole set is vertical-rules and not one booktabs grid prints here.

Three grids are two blocks side by side inside one frame - Tables 2, 4 and 7 each print their header band twice - so cols is the physical column count in each, and Table 2 is the widest object in the paper at 416.5 pt against a 418.3 pt measure, overhanging the right margin by about a point. Figure 6 is the one composite: a four-sided rule box divided at 276.2 pt into a typeset pseudo-code cell and a 356x500 bitmap flowchart cell, and the bitmap is a measured region of its own, recorded as a fragment of the frame rather than as a second exhibit. Its caption is the paper's only caption printed inside the box it names.

Defects recorded, not corrected: Figure 4 draws hundreds of nodes with hubs numbered 8 and 13 where the section counts 16 papers, and the page never reconciles the two; Figure 3 hangs a year axis under the art that no node sits on, so the publication-time claim has no scale behind it; Figure 1 claims 511 vertices and 18000 edges for a drawing that shows a few hundred discs and carries no node labels at all; Table 5's fourth header column prints the range C(S(0.5-0.95)) while the sentence setting the experiment says a random value from 0 to 1 and the sentence below the grid says 0.5 to 0.95; Table 6's score column mixes whole numbers with one- and three-place decimals and only three of its fifteen companies have a non-zero in-degree; Table 3's first header cell prints the two words 'In Degree' over one column; and the prose typos stand as printed, among them 'a vertex reprsents a paper', 'This graph do not only reflect the citation relation', 'There are 9 companies list in Table can be found in top 20', 'a vertex reprsents' and the caption 'the top 20 researches with highest importance'.
rules: every grid in this paper is a closed box - full-height vertical rules at every column boundary plus a horizontal rule on every row - so all seven tables are vertical-rules and the paper prints no booktabs grid at all [table.rule_style]

rows counts every printed row including the header band: Table 3's header over fifteen rank rows is sixteen, and the count comes from the number of horizontal rules minus one, not from the text layer's line order [table.rows]

cols counts the PHYSICAL grid, so a table set as two side-by-side blocks of the same columns and a table set as two (Rank, Company) pairs both print their header twice and take 6 and 4 columns respectively [table.cols]

a grid indented well inside the measure keeps width half: 56 to 71 per cent of the local 417 to 427 pt measure, while the two flush grids at 85 and 99.6 per cent are full, and the percentage is named in each note [table.width]

a header cell that prints two words over what looks like one column is still one cell: 'In Degree' sits entirely inside the 181.0 to 233.0 pt column and the grid keeps 4 columns, not 5 [table.header_rows]

fixed decimal places are not decimal alignment: Table 1's three-decimal values are left-aligned and Table 6's mixed-precision scores are centred, so both are decimal_aligned false while Table 2's two-decimal columns are true [table.decimal_aligned]

the measured box is the exhibit even when the box holds typeset text beside art: Figure 6's region is the whole four-sided rule box, 84.4 to 511.1 pt, because that box is what the caption owns [table.note_sentence]

captions follow the exhibit type without exception - every figure caption prints below its art and every table caption above its grid - and Figure 6 is the single exception, its caption printed INSIDE the box at the bottom of the right cell [caption.position]

captions print the number with a colon and a lowercase gloss, 'Figure 6: the flowsheet of the algorithms', so numbering is Figure N: and Table N: throughout and no caption names a variable [caption.numbering]

a caption that names its own subject wrongly is recorded as printed and the mismatch goes into the item note; Figure 4's caption calls a drawing of hundreds of nodes the network of the 16 papers [caption.verbatim]
a grid the prose never numbers by number is still a table row: Table 2 is reached with 'The table below lists', Table 5 with 'Table shows' and Table 7 with 'in Table', all unnamed [mention.count]

a lowercase by-name citation is recorded as it prints, case-sensitively: 'show them in table 1' and 'list in table 4' are style 'table 1' and 'table 4' and would not match a capitalised spelling [mention.style]

an exhibit cited more than once keeps the FIRST citing page in first_page and counts the citations, so Figure 1 carries count 2 with lead_pages 0 even though its second citation is two pages later [mention.lead_pages]

two panels that differ in what they draw - typeset pseudo-code beside a drawn flowchart - are composite-panel with panel_count 2, while two node-link drawings of the same family stay one row [geometry.panel_count]
a bitmap measured inside a ruled frame is a fragment of that exhibit, not a second one: Figure 6's flowchart is excluded fragment-of-other and only the frame is a row [place.section_numbered]

the heading detector reads a display-set algorithm block and a table's printed rows as headings, so every section_path here is the printed label of the heading that governs the region and never the nearest detector record [place.page_zone]
